Cagrilintide: The Amylin Analog Powering CagriSema's Record Phase 3 Weight Loss — Research Dossier

Medical Disclaimer: Research compounds discussed for educational purposes only. Cagrilintide and CagriSema are investigational compounds not approved by the FDA for any indication as of November 2026. No information here constitutes medical advice. Consult a healthcare provider before any clinical decision.

What Is Cagrilintide?

Cagrilintide (development code: AM833) is a long-acting amylin analog developed by Novo Nordisk — a once-weekly subcutaneous peptide that works through a fundamentally different mechanism than GLP-1 drugs like semaglutide or tirzepatide. While the entire obesity drug landscape has converged on GLP-1 receptor agonism, cagrilintide targets amylin receptors: a distinct satiety circuit in the brainstem that operates independently of — and additively with — the GLP-1 pathway.

The practical result: when cagrilintide is combined with semaglutide 2.4 mg as the fixed-dose combination CagriSema, Phase 3 clinical trials show 20.4–22.7% mean body weight reduction at 68 weeks — the highest efficacy figure for a fixed-dose obesity combination in peer-reviewed Phase 3 data, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2025.

Novo Nordisk submitted a New Drug Application (NDA) to the FDA for CagriSema in December 2025. An FDA decision is expected in late 2026 or early 2027.

What Is Amylin — and Why Does This Mechanism Matter?

Amylin (also called islet amyloid polypeptide, IAPP) is a 37-amino acid peptide hormone secreted by pancreatic beta cells alongside insulin whenever you eat. While insulin handles blood glucose, amylin handles the other half of the postprandial response:

  • Signals satiety to the brainstem — via the area postrema and nucleus tractus solitarius, different from GLP-1's arcuate hypothalamus and vagal targets
  • Slows gastric emptying — independent of GLP-1R signaling
  • Suppresses postprandial glucagon — reducing hepatic glucose output after meals
  • Reduces food intake — particularly portion size and eating rate

People with obesity have amylin resistance and elevated amylin secretion, similar to insulin resistance — the satiety signal stops working. Cagrilintide bypasses this by flooding amylin receptors with a potent, long-acting agonist regardless of endogenous amylin levels.

The key insight: because amylin receptors and GLP-1 receptors are in different brain regions and activate different signaling cascades, their combination produces additive satiety suppression rather than redundant overlap. This is why CagriSema outperforms either component alone by a wide margin.

Mechanism of Action: Brainstem Amylin Circuit

Amylin Receptor Complex

Amylin receptors are unique: they are heterodimers formed by pairing the calcitonin receptor (CTR) with receptor activity-modifying proteins (RAMPs):

  • AMY1R = CTR + RAMP1
  • AMY2R = CTR + RAMP2
  • AMY3R = CTR + RAMP3

These receptors are most densely expressed in the area postrema (AP) — a circumventricular organ that sits outside the blood-brain barrier and directly samples the bloodstream — and in the adjacent nucleus tractus solitarius (NTS), a key brainstem hub for satiety and energy balance. By contrast, GLP-1R agonists primarily work through vagal afferents and arcuate hypothalamic circuits. The two pathways converge downstream but are anatomically and pharmacologically distinct going in.

Amylin Receptor Agonism Effects

  • Reduces meal size and caloric intake via brainstem satiety signaling
  • Extends gastric emptying time (independent of GLP-1R)
  • Suppresses postprandial glucagon secretion from alpha cells
  • Modulates insulin sensitivity and glucose disposal through non-GLP-1 pathways
  • Works synergistically with GLP-1R agonism — documented in both animal pharmacology and Phase 3 human trials

Key Research Findings

Phase 3 REDEFINE 1 — NEJM 2025 (Flagship Trial)

REDEFINE 1 (NCT05669755) is the definitive Phase 3 randomized controlled trial for cagrilintide in obesity. Enrollment: >3,400 adults with obesity (BMI ≥30) or overweight (BMI ≥27 with weight-related comorbidity), no T2D. Duration: 68 weeks. This was a 3-arm trial:

Treatment Arm Mean Weight Loss at 68 Weeks
Cagrilintide 2.4 mg (monotherapy) −11.8%
Semaglutide 2.4 mg (monotherapy) ~−15% (SUSTAIN/STEP benchmark)
CagriSema 2.4 mg / 2.4 mg −20.4% to −22.7%
Placebo −2.3%

The cagrilintide monotherapy result — 11.8% at 68 weeks — marks the first Phase 3 randomized controlled trial of a long-acting amylin analog as an obesity monotherapy, establishing a new drug class benchmark. The CagriSema combination result (20–22%) confirms the additive hypothesis.

Phase 3 REIMAGINE Program in Type 2 Diabetes (Lancet Family, 2026)

Three Phase 3 trials evaluated CagriSema in T2D, all published in peer-reviewed journals in 2026:

Trial Journal Duration HbA1c Reduction
REIMAGINE 1 Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinol 40 weeks −1.80%
REIMAGINE 2 Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinol 68 weeks −1.91%
REIMAGINE 3 The Lancet 2026;408:38–51 40 weeks −2.33%

REIMAGINE 5 / REDEFINE 9 Topline (September 21, 2026)

Novo Nordisk announced topline results on September 21, 2026 showing CagriSema superior to tirzepatide for weight loss in a head-to-head Phase 3 comparison. CagriSema 1.0 mg/1.0 mg achieved:

  • 21.0% weight loss in adults with overweight/obesity
  • 12.4% weight loss in type 2 diabetes subgroup

Peer-reviewed publication pending as of November 2026.

How Cagrilintide Compares to the Obesity Drug Landscape

Drug Mechanism Phase 3 Weight Loss Status
Semaglutide 2.4 mg (Wegovy) GLP-1R ~15% (STEP 1) FDA Approved
Tirzepatide 15 mg (Zepbound) GLP-1R + GIPR ~21% (SURMOUNT-1) FDA Approved
Retatrutide 12 mg GLP-1R + GIPR + GCGR ~24–28% (TRIUMPH) Phase 3 (NDA pending)
CagriSema 2.4/2.4 mg GLP-1R + AMY 20–22% (REDEFINE 1) NDA Filed (FDA Dec 2025)
Cagrilintide 2.4 mg (mono) AMY receptors only 11.8% (REDEFINE 1) Phase 3 (RENEW, 2026)

All Phase 3 figures are from individual trials and not head-to-head comparisons unless specified. REIMAGINE 5 is the exception: a direct head-to-head versus tirzepatide showing CagriSema superiority (topline only, not yet peer-reviewed).

Dosing in Clinical Trials

  • Administration: Once-weekly subcutaneous injection
  • Phase 3 doses: 0.5 mg, 1.0 mg, and 2.4 mg weekly; dose escalation schedule used (consistent with standard incretin drug titration over 20–24 weeks)
  • CagriSema: fixed-dose combination of cagrilintide 2.4 mg + semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly
  • IMPORTANT: Cagrilintide and CagriSema are investigational. Doses used outside of clinical trials are not approved, validated, or available outside research settings

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How is cagrilintide different from amycretin, semaglutide, and other obesity peptides?

Cagrilintide targets a completely different receptor system than GLP-1 drugs. Semaglutide and liraglutide activate only GLP-1 receptors; tirzepatide adds GIP receptor agonism; retatrutide adds glucagon receptor agonism on top of GLP-1 and GIP. Cagrilintide activates amylin receptors — the same receptors the pancreatic hormone amylin binds — which are concentrated in the area postrema and nucleus tractus solitarius of the brainstem, a distinct neural circuit from the GLP-1-targeted arcuate hypothalamus and vagal pathways.

This non-overlapping mechanism makes amylin agonism additive to GLP-1 agonism: when cagrilintide is combined with semaglutide as CagriSema, Phase 3 weight loss reaches 20–22%, well above either drug alone. Amycretin is a different Novo Nordisk compound — a single-molecule oral peptide that chemically fuses GLP-1 and amylin receptor activity into one chain (Phase 1 only as of November 2026). Cagrilintide is a pure amylin analog injected weekly; it is combined with semaglutide as a separate drug, not fused with it.

Q: What do the REDEFINE Phase 3 trials show for cagrilintide?

REDEFINE 1 (n > 3,400 adults with obesity, 68 weeks, NEJM 2025) is the flagship Phase 3 trial. It included cagrilintide 2.4 mg monotherapy (−11.8% weight loss vs −2.3% placebo) and CagriSema 2.4/2.4 mg (−20.4% to −22.7%). This establishes cagrilintide as the first long-acting amylin analog with Phase 3 efficacy data in obesity, and CagriSema as one of the highest-efficacy fixed-dose obesity drug combinations in peer-reviewed Phase 3 data. The REIMAGINE program added three more Phase 3 trials in T2D (all published in Lancet-family journals in 2026), showing HbA1c reductions of 1.8–2.3%. REIMAGINE 5 topline (September 2026) showed CagriSema superior to tirzepatide in head-to-head weight loss, though peer-review is pending.

Q: What is the regulatory and approval timeline for cagrilintide in 2026–2027?

Novo Nordisk filed an NDA for CagriSema (cagrilintide 2.4 mg + semaglutide 2.4 mg) for chronic weight management with the FDA in December 2025. The standard 12-month FDA review places a decision around December 2026 to Q1 2027. If approved, CagriSema would be the first amylin-mechanism weight management drug approved since pramlintide (Symlin, 2005). Standalone cagrilintide is in Phase 3 investigation via the RENEW program (initiated 2026), with results likely 3–4 years away. Neither compound is currently FDA-approved. Research compounds discussed for educational purposes. Not FDA-approved for human use. Consult a healthcare provider before use.

Research Limitations

  • CagriSema is not FDA-approved; regulatory approval is pending and not guaranteed
  • Some Phase 3 efficacy figures vary across sources (20.4% vs 22.7% for REDEFINE 1 CagriSema arm); consult primary NEJM publication for authoritative data
  • REIMAGINE 5 (the head-to-head vs tirzepatide) is topline company data only; peer-reviewed publication pending as of November 2026
  • Long-term cardiovascular safety of CagriSema is under investigation in REDEFINE 3 (cardiovascular outcomes trial); results not yet available
  • Adverse events (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation) during dose titration are consistent with GLP-1-class drugs; long-term amylin receptor-specific effects require further study
  • Cagrilintide monotherapy Phase 3 (RENEW program) results are years away; the 11.8% monotherapy figure comes from one arm of REDEFINE 1
  • No published data on effects in special populations (CKD, hepatic impairment) for cagrilintide specifically
